audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: 2 Chronicles 27: Jotham's reign (16 years). Abbreviated parallel to 2 Kings 15:32-38 (not in 2 Chronicles counterpart structure). Emphasizes building, military success, and sustained moral uprightness without temple entry. Closure narrative precedes Ahaz's dramatic failure. Source-text is stable; Hebrew witnesses consistent.

verses.restored: Jotham was twenty and five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah, daughter of Zadok.

familiar.text: Jotham was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.

notes.title: Age formula
notes.body: Parallel to 2 Kings 15:33; source repeats age/reign span in v. 8.

modern.text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יוֹתָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְרוּשָׁ֖ה בַּת צָדֽוֹק

verses.restored: He did what was right before YHWH, according to all that his father Uzziah did; except he did not enter the temple of YHWH. And the people were still acting corruptly.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the LORD. And the people did yet corruptly.

notes.title: Temple exclusion
notes.body: Crucial distinction: unlike Uzziah (2 Chr 26:16–18), Jotham maintains proper boundaries. His avoidance is restraint, not judgment.

modern.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done. In addition, he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still behaved corruptly.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֜ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה כְּכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו רַ֕ק לֹא בָ֖א אֶל הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה וְע֥וֹד הָעָ֖ם מַשְׁחִיתִֽים

verses.restored: He built the upper gate of the house of YHWH, and on the wall of Ophel he built extensively.

familiar.text: He built the high gate of the house of the LORD, and on the wall of Ophel he built much.

modern.text: Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he worked extensively on the wall at the hill of Ophel.

original.text: ה֗וּא בָּנָ֛ה אֶת שַׁ֥עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה הָעֶלְי֑וֹן וּבְחוֹמַ֥ת הָעֹ֛פֶל בָּנָ֖ה לָרֹֽב

verses.restored: Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built fortified residences and towers.

familiar.text: Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built castles and towers.

modern.text: He also built cities in the hill country of Judah and fortresses and towers in the forests.

original.text: וְעָרִ֥ים בָּנָ֖ה בְּהַר יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבֶחֳרָשִׁ֣ים בָּנָ֔ה בִּֽירָנִיּ֖וֹת וּמִגְדָּלִֽים

verses.restored: He also fought against the king of the Ammonites and grew mighty over them. The Ammonites gave him in that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand measures of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same tribute in the second year and the third.

familiar.text: He fought also with the king of the Ammonites, and prevailed against them. And the children of Ammon gave him the same year an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. So much did the children of Ammon pay unto him, both the second year, and the third.

notes.title: Tribute sequence
notes.body: Ammonite payments continue; 'second year and third' likely indicates sustained payment pattern, not a single triennium.

modern.text: Jotham waged war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them, and that year they gave him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. They paid him the same in the second and third years.

original.text: וְ֠הוּא נִלְחַ֞ם עִם מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן֮ וַיֶּחֱזַ֣ק עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וַיִּתְּנוּ ל֨וֹ בְנֵֽי עַמּ֜וֹן בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא מֵאָה֙ כִּכַּר כֶּ֔סֶף וַעֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֤ים כֹּרִים֙ חִטִּ֔ים וּשְׂעוֹרִ֖ים עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים זֹ֗את הֵשִׁ֤יבוּ לוֹ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית וְהַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית

familiar.text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God.

modern.text: So Jotham grew powerful because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.

familiar.text: He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

notes.title: Repetition
notes.body: Source repeats v. 1 data (age, reign length); common in royal chronicles to bracket the narrative with confirming formula.

modern.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: And Jotham lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.

notes.title: Succession notice
notes.body: Ahaz's reign (ch. 28) marks sharp moral inversion: idolatry, temple violation, child sacrifice.

modern.text: And Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Ahaz reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹתָם֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

translation_notes: Verse 2: 'did the right' (הַיָּשָׁר) preserves stronger sense than 'did that which was right'; parallels his father's reign but marks critical distinction: no temple access despite public sanctity.
Verse 5: Ammonite tribute appears in two sequential years; Hebrew construction '(בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְׁנִית וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁית)' suggests first occurrence + repeat pattern rather than three years total.
Verse 6: 'prepared his ways' (הֵכִין דְּרָכָיו) is active moral-spiritual commitment language, not passive virtue.
source_witness_audit_flags: Verse 5: Tribute sequence grammar ('second year and the third')—verify against 2 Kings 15:37b and Ammonite historical context if available.
